rows.selection_reason: No experiments are completed, so the key uncertainty is whether a simple RNA-only model provides a useful baseline before adding multiprofile aggregation, image modality, or fusion. This tests the minimal single-profile PCA RNA configuration and gives a low-confounding anchor for later comparisons of profile setting, image-only baselines, and multimodal fusion. It is the best next step under limited budget because it is simple, cheap, and reduces uncertainty about whether more complex design choices are needed.

The only completed experiment is a simple RNA-only single-profile PCA baseline with validation accuracy 0.485, leaving major uncertainty about whether the image modality contains useful predictive signal. config_010 tests an image-only single-profile ResNet50 baseline, changing mainly the modality while keeping the profile setting simple and avoiding aggregation/fusion confounds. This is the best next use of budget because it establishes whether image features are competitive before investing in multimodal fusion or more complex multiprofile/aggregation settings.

RNA single-profile PCA is currently much stronger than image ResNet (accuracy 0.485 vs 0.208; F1 0.464 vs 0.172), so RNA is the more promising direction. The key uncertainty is whether multiprofile aggregation can improve the RNA representation without changing the encoder. config_002 keeps the same pca_n2000 RNA encoder and adds only multiprofile avgpool, the simplest aggregation option, directly testing the profile/aggregation effect. It is a low-complexity extension of the current best baseline and will clarify whether multiprofile settings are worth pursuing before testing transformer aggregation or multimodal fusion.

The strongest evidence so far is that multiprofile RNA with PCA and avgpool (config_002) substantially outperforms single-profile RNA and image-only ResNet, indicating that profile aggregation is an important design choice. The key uncertainty is whether transformer aggregation can improve over avgpool for the same multiprofile PCA representation. config_003 changes only aggregation, isolating that effect while building directly on the current best configuration. This is a better use of the next experiment than changing encoder or adding image modality because it tests a minimal, high-value extension of the most promising result.

The strongest evidence so far is that RNA-only multiprofile with PCA and avgpool is the best configuration (0.591 accuracy, 0.573 F1), clearly outperforming single-profile PCA and transformer aggregation, while image-only ResNet is weak. This makes RNA representation the most promising next design choice to exploit. config_005 tests whether a learned RNA encoder (scVI) improves over PCA while keeping the best-known multiprofile avgpool setting fixed, providing a clean comparison to config_002 and reducing uncertainty about representation quality before moving to more complex multimodal fusion.

RNA-only multiprofile scvi_n200 with avgpool is currently the best result (0.650 accuracy, 0.628 F1), while image-only models are weak and PCA-based RNA models show that multiprofile avgpool can help. This experiment tests whether the scvi_n200 gain is mainly due to the encoder itself or to multiprofile aggregation by evaluating the same encoder in a singleprofile setting. It is a simple one-factor comparison that reduces uncertainty about profile complexity before spending budget on transformer aggregation or multimodal fusion.

RNA-only multiprofile models with avgpool are currently strongest, and scvi_n200 outperforms pca_n2000 under the same setting, while image-only evidence is weak. The key remaining uncertainty on the RNA side is whether the untested scgpt encoder can improve on scvi_n200 when profile setting and aggregation are held at their currently best values. config_008 tests this single-factor representation comparison, isolating encoder choice without adding image or fusion complexity. Under a limited budget, this exploits the strong multiprofile/avgpool evidence while efficiently exploring an important design choice before moving to more complex multimodal configurations.

The strongest evidence so far is that RNA-only multiprofile models outperform image-only models, and the best completed configuration is config_005: scvi_n200 + multiprofile + avgpool with validation accuracy 0.650 and F1 0.628. For PCA multiprofile, avgpool outperformed transformer, but that comparison has not yet been made for the best encoder, scvi_n200. config_006 changes only the aggregation method from avgpool to transformer while keeping the same RNA encoder and multiprofile setting, directly testing whether transformer aggregation can improve on the current best RNA representation. This is the best next experiment because it is a controlled extension of the most promising direction, may identify a higher-performing configuration, and clarifies whether aggregation choice matters for the strongest RNA encoder before spending budget on more complex multimodal fusion.

Existing evidence strongly favors RNA-based multiprofile models, with scvi_n200 + multiprofile + transformer/avgpool reaching ~0.65 validation accuracy, while image-only ResNet50 singleprofile is very weak (~0.21). This leaves a key uncertainty: whether the image modality is intrinsically uninformative or whether the tested image encoder is too weak. config_013 tests image-only singleprofile with imagenet_vit_l, directly comparing image representation while keeping the profile setting unchanged. If it improves substantially, it justifies later tests of image multiprofile aggregation and multimodal fusion; if it remains weak, it suggests image features are not currently useful and budget should stay focused on RNA or other design choices. This is the best next experiment because it reduces a major source of uncertainty with minimal confounding before adding aggregation or fusion complexity.

The strongest completed model is RNA-only scvi_n200 with multiprofile and transformer aggregation (config_006, 0.653 acc / 0.628 F1), while image-only models are much weaker, leaving the key uncertainty as whether image features add complementary value under fusion. This experiment tests that directly by adding the slightly stronger ViT image branch to the best RNA settings while keeping profile setting and aggregation fixed, using simple concat fusion as a baseline. It is the best next use of budget because it isolates the multimodal extension from confounds like weighted fusion or weaker RNA/image choices, and it will clarify whether fusion is worth further exploration.
